To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

syndecan, a cell surface receptor for extracellular matrix and growth factors, is expressed in some, but not all, human myeloma tumors and regulates myeloma cell interactions with the bone marrow stroma.
syndecan is expressed by human myeloma tumor cells and that this expression correlates with adhesion to type 1 collagen.
syndecan is expressed on the surface of human myeloma and binds to the stromal extracellular matrix.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the extracellular matrix (ECM) in regulating the behavior of myeloma cells.
the expression, structure and function of syndican on human myelomacell lines and myelomapatient bone marrow cells.
the expression, structure and function of the syndecans on human myelomas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
syndecan regulates myeloma cell binding to the bone marrow microenvironment and is expressed by the well-differentiated myeloma cells.
syndecan is expressed by myeloma plasma cells and that it regulates their adhesion to bone marrow stroma via interaction with collagen.
syndecan is expressed on the surface of human myeloma and that syndecan functions to mediate adhesion of myeloma cells to type I collagen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the syndecans are a novel family of integral membrane proteins that are expressed by a wide variety of cell types and regulate cell behaviors by acting as matrix receptors, growth factor receptors, or both.
syndecan-1 is expressed by myeloma cells and is involved in the adhesion of myeloma cells to the bone marrow stroma.
syndecan is expressed on myeloma cells and that it binds to type I collagen, which is a major component of the bone marrow stroma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
syndecan-1 is expressed by human myeloma bone marrow cells and is required for adhesion of these cells to collagen type I, a component of the extracellular matrix of the bone marrow stroma.
syndecan-1 is a marker of myeloma cell differentiation and is expressed by the majority of myeloma cells in the bone marrow of patients with multiple myeloma.
syndecan is not a marker for myeloma cells in general, but rather a marker for a subset of myeloma cells with a well differentiated phenotype.
